title: This iPhone App Turns Your Lost Scrolling Hours Black
summary:
Your phone can quietly eat up hours. A new iPhone app called Oh My Hours tries to show that lost time. It turns each day into a row of circles, with one circle for every hour. If you spend time in an app you picked as a distraction, that hour's circle turns black.

You choose the distractions yourself. You can pick whole groups, like social media apps and games, or pick apps one by one. By default, even a few seconds in a distracting app can mark the whole hour as lost. A looser rule could tempt you to sneak in a little scrolling after each hour resets.

You can start using Oh My Hours for free on iOS. There is no sign of an Android version yet. Paying $10 a year or $20 for lifetime access lets you change the rules and see month and year views. You can also set quiet hours and reset an hour marked by mistake. One glance at the black circles shows whether the day went to scrolling, or to something better.
why_it_matters: It can help you notice when games or social media are eating up time you could spend playing, reading, or doing homework.

keywords.explanation: A distraction is something that pulls your attention away from what you are doing.
By default means what happens unless you change the setting.
To tempt someone means to make them want to do something even when they should not.
Lifetime means lasting for your whole life, or for as long as something exists.
iOS is the software system that runs on an iPhone.

background_read: A phone app can keep track of how time is spent, turning each hour into a simple picture that is easy to see at a glance.
People choose the apps that distract them, like social media apps and games, so they can notice when scrolling takes over time meant for other things.
Seeing lost time in a clear way can help people make a different choice about how they spend their day.
